item.text: The workspace is essentially empty, so I’m creating a single portable HTML file. I’m using FRED’s SP500 daily-close series as the live source, aggregating it to month-end in the browser, and embedding a recent snapshot so the dashboard still works if the live request is unavailable.

The first implementation is in place: controls, responsive SVG chart, scenario table, diagnostics, CSV import, and live refresh are all wired into one file. I’m moving into validation now—checking JavaScript syntax, rendering the page headlessly, and exercising the live/fallback data path.

item.text:
Built and validated the interactive dashboard:

[Open `sp500-forecast-dashboard.html`](</tmp/benchmark-real-ai-gpt-5.6-luna-xhigh-X6yH7U/sp500-forecast-dashboard.html>)

It includes:

- Trend + momentum forecasting model
- Adjustable lookback, horizon, model, and volatility regime
- Actual vs. forecast chart with 80% uncertainty range
- Scenario table and walk-forward diagnostics
- CSV upload support
- Embedded offline snapshot with optional FRED refresh

Data source: [FRED S&P 500 series](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SP500). The dashboard was syntax-checked, rendered in Chrome, and tested interactively.
